review_notes: I read the whole file. It has no @[simp] attributes. I also read the downstream files ColorLabelMachine.lean and RandomizedZeroBranch.lean, and grepped the KMedianRecovery directory for uses of label and color. The only simp-interface problem I found is that `label` and `color` have no projection or value lemmas, so users unfold them by hand. I did not recommend simp attributes for `colorMass_values`, `distinctMass_zero` or the other lemmas. They are applied with rw or are only used locally, and `colorMass_values` has an `if` right-hand side that would add case splits. I did not run Lean, so I make no claim that the proposed lemmas compile or that any simp behaviour was observed.

findings.excerpt:
def label (b : ℕ) (hb : 0 < b) (x : Fin (labelRange b)) : Fin b :=
  ⟨x.val % b, Nat.mod_lt _ hb⟩
findings.problem: `label` is a plain def, and `color` (lines 118–119) is a plain def. Neither has a value or projection simp lemma, such as `(label b hb x).val = x.val % b` or `(color x).val = if x.val < 2 then 0 else if x.val = 2 then 1 else 2`. Downstream code therefore has to unfold the definitions by name. ColorLabelMachine.lean does this in `colorWord_bits` with `unfold colorWord ColorLabel.color`, and in `labels_tensor` with a `simp only [..., ColorLabel.label, ...]` call. Unfolding is a blunt tool. `ColorLabel.label` is unfolded to its anonymous-constructor body, so the `x.val % b` form has to be re-derived each time. In this file, `labelMass_lower` shows `label b hb x = j` by `Fin.ext` followed by `Nat.mod_eq_of_lt`, which relies on defeq with the structure body.
findings.proposed_change: Add `@[simp] lemma label_val (b hb x) : (label b hb x).val = x.val % b := rfl`. Add `color_val` for the nested `if` on `x.val`, or better, add the four value lemmas `color_zero`, `color_one`, `color_two`, `color_three` (stated for the `Fin 4` literals) as `@[simp]`. Downstream proofs can then use `simp [ColorLabel.label_val]`, or a plain `simp`, instead of unfolding the definitions. `colorMass_values` could also use the `color` lemmas in place of `norm_num [color, Fin.ext_iff]`.
findings.benefit: Users get one canonical normal form, `x.val % b`, for label values and explicit values for `color` on literals. They no longer unfold the definitions in `simp only` lists, and proofs depend less on how the definitions are written. Each rule is a terminating rewrite from a projection of an opaque-looking def to arithmetic, so it does not risk a loop or competing rules.
